title: Meet the Dinosaurs

subtitle.text: Reporter: Wow!
Look at those big plates on your back.
Who are you? Stegosaurus:
Hello there! I'm a Stegosaurus. My
name means roof lizard. Reporter: Why
are you called a roof lizard? Stegosaurus:
That name came from my back plates. Scientists
thought they were stacked like roof tiles. Reporter:
But your plates are not lying flat. Stegosaurus:
Right. Now everyone knows they stand up tall.
They look like big flags along my back. Reporter:
How big are you? Stegosaurus:
I'm about nine meters long.
That's almost as long as a school bus. Reporter:
Your tail has spikes! Stegosaurus:
That's right. My
sharp tail spikes scare away enemies. Reporter:
Do you eat meat? Stegosaurus:
Nope. I'm a peaceful plant eater. I
love soft plants and leaves.
Reporter: What year is it now?
Stegosaurus: We are 150 million years before your
time. This is the Jurassic period.
Reporter: Tell me about your Jurassic neighbors.
Stegosaurus: I have good neighbors like
Brachiosauruses. And there are bad ones like Allosauruses.
Reporter: It was great meeting you, Stegosaurus.
Stegosaurus: It was fun talking to you, little
reporter. Come visit again!
Reporter: Hey! Brachiosaurus! Hey, wait a second!
Ugh . . . ugh . . . Hello! I'm a reporter.
Can I interview you? Brachiosaurus:
Hello, there. I'm a Brachiosaurus.
My name means arm lizard. Reporter:
Arm lizard? That's a funny name!
Brachiosaurus: It is!
My front legs, or arms, are very long. They're
longer than my back legs. Reporter:
Are you heavier than an elephant? Brachiosaurus:
Of course. I weigh much more than one.
I weigh as much as eight elephants! Reporter:
Wow! That's really heavy.
Do you eat meat? Brachiosaurus:
Nope! I'm a plant eater. I
munch on leaves and twigs. Reporter:
Your neck is really long! It's
like a giraffe's. Brachiosaurus: Yes,
I can eat from the tallest trees. Reporter:
Who's taller: you or a giraffe? Brachiosaurus:
I'm more than twice as tall.
I'm one of the biggest dinosaurs. Reporter:
Wow! This is the Jurassic period, right?
Brachiosaurus: Yes.
We are 150 million years before your time. Reporter:
What other dinosaurs do you live with?
Brachiosaurus: Apatosauruses and Stegosauruses are my friends.
Reporter: That's wild!
Thanks for chatting, Brachiosaurus!
Brachiosaurus: Anytime, little reporter. Come back soon!
Reporter: You look scary!
Who are you? Tyrannosaurus:
I'm a Tyrannosaurus.
Tyrannosaurus: You may call me Tyrannosaurus rex.
That means tyrant lizard king.
Reporter: Are you the king of dinosaurs?
Tyrannosaurus: Ha-ha! I got my name because of my
size. I'm one of the biggest meat eaters ever!
Reporter: How big are you?
Tyrannosaurus: I'm about 12 meters
long. That's longer than a school bus.
Reporter: But your arms look really
short. Tyrannosaurus: That's okay. I'm a fierce
hunter. And I don't need my arms to
hunt. Reporter: Your head is the size of a
bathtub. Tyrannosaurus: Yes. My head
is big. My big head holds my very big
mouth. My powerful bite can crush
bones. Reporter: How many teeth do you
have? Tyrannosaurus: I have sixty
teeth! Some are longer than large
bananas. Reporter: Yikes. What year is it
now? Tyrannosaurus: We are seventy million years before
your time. This is the Cretaceous
period. Tyrannosaurus: Ooh—I see my next
meal! Reporter: I hope it's
not me. Tyrannosaurus: You're too small,
little reporter. There's a yummy
Triceratops. And an
Edmontosaurus. It's time to hunt!
Reporter: Whoa! Your horns are amazing.
Triceratops: Thank you. I'm a
Triceratops. My name means three horned face.
Reporter: That name is perfect for
you. Triceratops: Yes. Look at the horns above my
eyes. They are one meter long.
Reporter: What do you use your horns
for? Triceratops: I can use them to attack
enemies. Sometimes Triceratops fight each other
too. Reporter: Your head looks very
fancy. Triceratops: Thanks! I love to show off
my frill. I can use it to protect my
neck. Reporter: How big are
you? Triceratops: I'm nine
meters long. I'm almost as long as a school
bus. Reporter: What do
you eat? Triceratops: I eat plants that
grow low. My teeth are good at slicing
tough plants. I have eight hundred
teeth. Reporter: That's a
lot! Triceratops: Yes, but you can't see
them all. I am always growing new
teeth. New teeth grow under my old teeth.
Reporter: Are we in the Cretaceous
period? Triceratops: That's
right. We are seventy million years before your
time. Triceratops: Oh! A Tyrannosaurus is
coming. Tyrannosauruses aren't friendly.
Reporter: Be careful!
Triceratops: Don't worry. I can fight
back. Good-bye, little reporter.
Reporter: Whoa! You look like a tank!
Ankylosaurus: I'm not a tank! I'm an
Ankylosaurus. My name means stiff lizard.
Reporter: How did you get that name?
Ankylosaurus: Some of my bones are joined together
tightly. This makes my body stiff and strong.
Reporter: What are those things on your
back? Ankylosaurus: They are hard, bony
plates. This armor protects my back and neck.
Reporter: You have a club on your
tail. Ankylosaurus: Yes. My tail club is a powerful
weapon. I can break enemies’ bones with one
swing! Reporter: Why do you need a weapon like
that? Ankylosaurus: I move slowly, and my brain
is small. I'm an easy target for enemies like
Tyrannosauruses. But they can't eat me easily!
Reporter: Oh! You live with
Tyrannosaurus. Ankylosaurus:
Yes. We are seventy million years before your time.
This is the Cretaceous period.
Reporter: How heavy are you?
Ankylosaurus: I weigh more than an elephant.
I eat as much as one too.
Reporter: What do you eat?
Ankylosaurus: I eat plants that grow low.
I can't lift my head very high.
Reporter: Do you—
Ankylosaurus: Sorry. I'm going to a fern patch.
I walk slowly, so I'd better go now.
Reporter: Bye, Ankylosaurus!
Ankylosaurus: Good-bye, little reporter.
Reporter: Hello! Who are you?
Iguanodon: I'm an
Iguanodon. Reporter: Are you an
iguana? Iguanodon: Ha-ha! No
way. But my teeth look like iguanas' teeth.
That's how I got my name.
Reporter: You're much bigger than an iguana!
Iguanodon: Yep.
I'm almost as long as a school bus.
My body is nine meters long. Reporter:
I don't see your teeth.
Iguanodon: They're in the back of my mouth.
I don't have any front teeth.
So I use my beak to tear plants. Reporter:
Your hands look cool. Iguanodon:
Thanks. I have long fingers that bend.
They help me grab things. And
my thumbs are sharp spikes. Reporter:
What do you use the spikes for? Iguanodon:
I use them as a weapon. I
can also break open seeds with them. Reporter:
Do you walk on two legs? Iguanodon:
I usually walk on four legs.
But I can also walk on two. Reporter:
Is this the Cretaceous period?
Iguanodon: Yes, it is.
We are 125 million years before your time. Reporter:
Whoa! That's a long time ago.
Iguanodon: You're right.
I live way before Tyrannosauruses and Triceratops. Reporter:
Thanks for talking with me, Iguanodon.
Iguanodon: Any time, little reporter.
Reporter: Hmm.
I don't see any dinosaurs in this desert.
Velociraptor: Hey! Down here!
I'm a Velociraptor. Reporter:
Oh, hello, little guy! Does
your name mean short dinosaur? Velociraptor:
No! My name means fast robber. Reporter:
Why are you called a fast robber?
Velociraptor: I can run about forty kilometers per hour.
That helps me grab food fast.
Reporter: Ooh! What do you eat?
Velociraptor: I'm a meat eater.
I have a long claw on each foot.
I use them like knives when I hunt. Reporter:
Can you fly?
Velociraptor: I have long feathers on my arms.
So my arms look like wings. But
I can't fly. Reporter:
Your tail is really long! Velociraptor:
It helps me balance when I move fast.
Reporter: How big are you?
Velociraptor: I'm two meters long.
I weigh as much as a medium dog.
Reporter: What period is this?
Velociraptor: This is the Cretaceous period.
We are 75 million years before your time.
Reporter: Do other dinosaurs live here?
Velociraptor: Yes. Oviraptors live
here. And so do yummy Protoceratops.
Oh. There's one now! Bye! Reporter:
Wow! You are fast! Good-bye!
Velociraptor: See you next time, little reporter!
Reporter: What kind of dinosaur are you?
Pteranodon: I'm not a
dinosaur! I'm a pterosaur—a flying reptile.
Reporter: Oh!
Well, then, what kind of pterosaur are you? Pteranodon:
I'm a Pteranodon.
My name means winged and toothless. Reporter:
Are you a good flier? Pteranodon:
Of course! I have light, hollow bones.
And my wings stretch seven meters wide. Reporter:
That's really wide! Pteranodon:
I use them to push off the ground.
Then I flap them to fly. Reporter:
Do you spend all your time flying? Pteranodon:
No. I like to float in water.
That's where I find my food. Reporter:
Oh. What do you eat? Pteranodon:
I catch fish with my beak.
Then I swallow them whole. But
I have to watch out for enemies. Reporter: Who
are your enemies? Pteranodon:
Water reptiles, sharks, and dinosaurs. I
have enemies on both land and water! Reporter: What
year is it now? Pteranodon:
I live 88 million years before your time. This
is the Cretaceous period. Reporter: You
live at the same time as dinosaurs. Pteranodon:
Yes. But don't call us dinosaurs, little reporter. Reporter:
I know that now! Thanks, Pteranodon!
Pteranodon: I'll be off now. Good-bye!
Reporter: You're really big!
Who are you? Spinosaurus:
I'm a Spinosaurus.
My name means spine lizard. Reporter:
Your spines are tall. Spinosaurus:
That's right. Some are almost two meters tall.
They hold up my sail. Reporter:
What is your sail for? Spinosaurus:
Scientists think I use it to show off.
Some think it controls my body heat. Reporter:
Hmm. Are those things true?
Spinosaurus: I'll never tell!
It's my spiny secret. Reporter:
Do you live near water?
Spinosaurus: Yes. I like to stay near the water.
My favorite food is fish. Reporter:
Oh. How do you catch fish?
Spinosaurus: I have jaws like a crocodile.
I snap them fast to catch food.
Reporter: How big are you?
Spinosaurus: I am 14 meters long.
I am one of the biggest meat eaters.
I am longer than a Tyrannosaurus. Reporter:
Do you live with Tyrannosauruses? Spinosaurus:
No. I live a long time before Tyrannosauruses.
Reporter: What year are we in?
Spinosaurus: We're one hundred million years before your
time. This is the Cretaceous period.
Spinosaurus: I'm going to splash in the river
now. Good-bye, little reporter.
Reporter: Good-bye, Spinosaurus!
Reporter: Aww! Those babies are cute.
Are you their mother?
Maiasaura: Yes. I am a Maiasaura.
That means good mother lizard. Reporter:
Why are you called a good mother?
Maiasaura: My babies cannot walk or find food.
So I must take good care of them.
Many other dinosaurs don't do this. Reporter:
There are so many Maiasaura here! Maiasaura:
Yes. Our herd has hundreds of dinosaurs!
This large group keeps us safe from enemies. Reporter:
Who are your enemies?
Maiasaura: Other dinosaurs sometimes attack us.
They try to eat our babies. Reporter:
What do you eat?
Maiasaura: I am a plant eater.
Reporter: Is that pile of plants your next
meal? Maiasaura: No. That's another Maiasaura's
nest. We cover our eggs with old plants.
This keeps our eggs warm.
Reporter: How big are you?
Maiasaura: I weigh as much as a hippo.
And I am nine meters long.
Reporter: How many legs do you walk on?
Maiasaura: I mainly walk on four
legs. Young Maiasaura walk on two legs.
Reporter: What year is it now?
Maiasaura: We are eighty million years before your
time. This is the Cretaceous period.
Maiasaura: I must feed my babies
now. Good-bye, little reporter.
Reporter: Good-bye, Maiasaura.
Reporter: Ahh! You scared me!
Elasmosaurus: Hello, I'm an Elasmosaurus.
Reporter: Wait. Are you a
dinosaur? Elasmosaurus: Nope. I'm a
plesiosaur. Plesiosaurs are reptiles that live in water.
Reporter: Your neck is so
long! Elasmosaurus: I'm ten meters
long. My neck is over half of my length.
And it has 72 bones.
Reporter: How do you use your neck?
Elasmosaurus: It helps me breathe when I swim.
And it helps me look for food.
Can I have that rock you're holding? Reporter:
Sure . . . Um, why did you swallow it?
Elasmosaurus: My teeth aren't good for chewing.
So I have to swallow food whole.
Rocks help grind food in my stomach. Reporter:
Oh. What do you eat? Elasmosaurus:
I eat fish and mollusks.
Reporter: What other creatures live here in the water?
Elasmosaurus: There are sharks, rays, turtles, and shellfish.
Other plesiosaurs live here too.
Reporter: Your flippers look like a sea turtle's.
Can you go on land? Elasmosaurus:
No. I can't use my flippers on land.
Reporter: What year is it?
Elasmosaurus: We are eighty million years before your
time. This is the Cretaceous period.
Uh-oh! I see a shark. Reporter:
Yikes! It's time to go. Elasmosaurus:
Good-bye, little reporter. Thanks for the rock!
Reporter: Good-bye, Elasmosaurus.
Reporter: Whoa! What a cool head!
Who are you?
Pachycephalosaurus: I am a Pachycephalosaurus.
That means thick headed lizard. Reporter:
Is that a helmet on your head?
Pachycephalosaurus: Well, it looks like a helmet.
But it's really a thick, bony dome.
It's the top part of my skull. Reporter:
You have some interesting knobs and spikes too.
Do you like to show off your head? Pachycephalosaurus:
Yes! My head shows I'm tough.
Reporter: I bet you're a good fighter!
Pachycephalosaurus: Yep. I fight other Pachycephalosaurus
sometimes. We use our heads to fight each other.
Reporter: Your legs look strong too.
Pachycephalosaurus: They
are. They help me run fast.
Reporter: You're not very big.
Pachycephalosaurus: I'm four meters
long. And I'm not very tall.
So I eat food close to the ground. Reporter:
What do you eat?
Pachycephalosaurus: My teeth are good for eating plants.
I also eat fruits and seeds.
Reporter: What other dinosaurs live here?
Pachycephalosaurus: Triceratops and Ankylosaurus are my neighbors.
Reporter: Aha. So we're in the Cretaceous
period. Pachycephalosaurus: That's
right. We are seventy million years before your
time. Oh. I see another Pachycephalosaurus.
Reporter: Uh-oh. Stay safe!
Pachycephalosaurus: Don't worry. I always use my
head! Good-bye, little reporter.
